title: A SURVEY ON FAIRNESS OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN E-COMMERCE: PROGRESS, APPLICATION, AND CHALLENGE
findings: LLMs can exhibit religious bias by demonstrating favoritism or discrimination towards individuals or groups based on their religious beliefs. This bias can originate from generating text that stereotypes or stigmatizes certain religions, promotes one religion over others, or misrepresents religious practices. The paper notes that LLMs not only learn biases present in training data but can also amplify them.

measurement_description: The paper discusses benchmarks that measure religious bias in open-ended text generation. Specifically, it mentions the evaluation of favoritism, discrimination, stereotypes, stigmatization, or misrepresentation of religious beliefs in the text generated by LLMs. It also refers to metrics that assess sentiment, toxicity, and regard in the model's completions for prompts describing religious populations.
